newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Hong Kong businesses to keep tax status.
newsitem.headline: China says Hong Kong businesses to keep tax status.

text.p: China said on Monday Hong Kong businessmen would retain preferential tax status for investments on the Chinese mainland after the British colony reverts to Beijing rule this year.

"After 1997, China's tax laws will not apply to the Special Administrative Region and Hong Kong compatriots will be able to continue to receive the preferential treatment given to foreign investors," the China Taxation News said.
"There will be no tax changes as a result of 1997," the newspaper said, referring to the handover.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule, becoming a Special Administrative Region, at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years as a British colony.
Hong Kong is entitled to maintain its own tax system after the handover but the status of the territory's residents in China is less clear.

China gives foreign investors lower tax rates than Chinese companies. Although Beijing says it is the rightful ruler of both Hong Kong and Taiwan, it treats businessmen from both places as foreigners.

Foreign businessmen, however, are made to pay a whole range of fees that are not required of local businessmen. They also must hire employees through special government agencies, boosting their operating costs.
The newspaper did not say whether these fees would still apply to Hong Kong businesses after the transfer of power.
